facts.raw_span: A female infant with history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia
was admitted for reinduction chemotherapy
Seventeen days after her last day of chemotherapy, while neutropenic, she became febrile
Patient had an indwelling catheter
Several vesicles with an erythematous base were observed on the lower back and left thigh
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa
Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis
Periodic acid-Schiff staining was negative for fungal elements
PCR testing for herpes simplex virus (HSV) and varicella zoster virus (VZV) were negative
CT scan with contrast of thorax and brain showed lesions in the liver and brain

concepts.why: The patient has vesicles with an erythematous base, and the microscopic examination shows focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa, which is consistent with bacillary angiomatosis.
The patient has lesions in the liver and brain, and the presence of vesicles with an erythematous base could be consistent with disseminated cat-scratch disease.
The patient is neutropenic and has become febrile, which is consistent with neutropenic sepsis.
The patient has an indwelling catheter and has become febrile, which is consistent with catheter-related bloodstream infection.
The patient has a history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia and is undergoing reinduction chemotherapy, which could be consistent with relapsed disease.
The patient has lesions in the liver and brain, and the microscopic examination shows numerous filamentous bacilli with septa, which is consistent with systemic nocardiosis.

It explains the presence of filamentous bacilli with septa and gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis, which is consistent with Nocardia infection, and the negative results for fungal elements and herpes simplex and varicella zoster viruses.

rationales.F05: Vesicles with an erythematous base are consistent with cutaneous manifestations of Bacillary angiomatosis and Cutaneous nocardiosis
rationales.F06: Filamentous bacilli with septa are characteristic of Nocardia species, supporting Systemic nocardiosis and Cutaneous nocardiosis
rationales.F07: Gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis are consistent with Nocardia species, supporting Systemic nocardiosis and Cutaneous nocardiosis
rationales.F10: Lesions in the liver and brain are consistent with disseminated infection, supporting Systemic nocardiosis and Bacillary angiomatosis

frontier_selector.rationale: Numerous filamentous bacilli with septa and gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis, along with lesions in the liver and brain, support systemic nocardiosis over cutaneous nocardiosis.
